region: Lycia and the Pisidian Highlands, south-west Turkey
title: Turkey — Lycia and the Pisidian Highlands, Coast Path to Snowline
subtitle: Twelve nights on the Lycian Way, drowned cities, a gas flame, and two mountain cities above the snowline
summary: A 13-day self-drive on Turkey's south-west coast and the Taurus above it, away from the Istanbul and Cappadocia circuit and clear of every official restricted zone. Lycian Way walking, tent nights at Çıralı, Kekova's sunken city and two mountain cities.
introduction: Thirteen days from Dalaman to Antalya along the Lycian coast, in a rented car with two drivers. Each day pairs a short drive with a walk on the Lycian Way, from the cliffs above Ölüdeniz to the rock tombs of Myra. Boats go over the sunken stairways of Kekova. Tents go up at Patara and Çıralı, where gas flames burn on the hillside at night. The route then turns inland to Termessos and Sagalassos, two Pisidian mountain cities near the snowline, and ends at the lake town of Eğirdir. March gives mild coast days and quiet sites.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is desert and wadis on empty tracks; this is a mountain-and-sea Mediterranean coast on waymarked footpaths and small Lycian harbour villages, with ruins on almost every day and snow within sight of the beach. Camping is in pension gardens, not wild desert.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package Turkey runs Istanbul, Cappadocia and Pamukkale on coaches. This route stays away from that circuit: small pensions, local boats, ruins with almost no visitors in March, and walking sections of the Lycian Way.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination offers a waymarked long-distance coastal footpath beside ancient Lycian ruins, tent nights at a natural eternal flame, and two Pisidian mountain cities at 1,000 and 1,500 m in the same fortnight.

duration.note: Day 1 and day 13 are flight days with arrival and departure on the Lycian coast.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Starts after Ramadan and the Eid holiday (about 9–11 March), the coast is mild (18–21 °C), the sea is about 17 °C and the Taurus sites are open or openable. February is cold and wet inland, and falls inside Ramadan.

februarySuitability.summary: Coast days reach about 16 °C, but rain is heaviest (about 113 mm in Antalya), Sagalassos and Eğirdir are often under snow, and Ramadan runs about 8 February to 9 March, which makes small-town restaurants less reliable by day.

marchSuitability.summary: Coast highs near 18 °C and rain easing; Sagalassos at 1,500 m may still hold snow in the first half of the month, so the inland section sits late in the route with a flexible day.

climate.regionNote: Antalya figures describe the coast; Eğirdir figures describe the Lake District at about 930 m. Sagalassos (about 1,500 m) is colder than both.

february.rainfall: About 113 mm at Antalya, mostly in short heavy storms
february.humidity: Moderate to high on the coast
february.notes: Eğirdir averages a high of 7 °C and a low of -0.3 °C.

march.notes: Eğirdir averages a high of 12 °C and a low of 2 °C; snow is very rare at Antalya.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Snow lies above about 1,500 m on the Lycian Way until early April. Sagalassos and the Taurus road can be snowed in; Termessos at 1,000 m is rarely blocked. Keep a flexible day.
climate.seaConditions: Sea about 17 °C in March (Antalya). Swimming is cold; boats run normally.
climate.airQuality: Good on the coast and in the highlands; no seasonal haze noted.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Spring flowers and early migrants; Patara nesting season starts later (May to September).

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Falls before the recommended March window; Eid al-Fitr about 9–11 March is just before it.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Nevruz
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Spring festival in the east and south-east; minor effect on this route.

climate.ramadan2027: Largely avoided by the 13–25 March window. For a February trip, daytime dining is limited in inland towns such as Ağlasun and Eğirdir, while Fethiye, Kaş and Antalya remain open. Eid al-Fitr crowds and prices apply around 9–11 March.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Lunar New Year has no effect on Turkey.
climate.tourismDemand: Very low on the Lycian coast in March; pensions and campsites are open on a reduced basis.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: March is low season for the Antalya region; fares are lowest outside Easter and school holidays.

geography.summary: A limestone coast of headlands and bays backed by the Taurus, with a gorge, a coastal cliff path, pine forests, a flaming hillside and a high mountain lake.
geography.distinctive: The Lycian Way runs from sea level to snow-capped ridges within a day's drive, and methane seeps burn at the Chimaera. No other coast in the portfolio combines these.

culturalHighlights.description: Pisidian city on a mountain shelf at 1,000 m that resisted Alexander.

culturalHighlights.name: Sagalassos

culturalHighlights.name: Pension and fish-village meals

adventureHighlights.name: Saklıkent gorge walk

adventureHighlights.name: Snow-dependent mountain cities

signatureExperiences.title: Lycian Way on the cliffs above Ölüdeniz and Kaş
signatureExperiences.description: Two stages on the waymarked footpath, about 4 h each, between cliffs and sea.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A marked long-distance coastal path beside Lycian ruins; none of the portfolio's other coasts has one.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Self-guided with a printed map; taxi back for the car. Guide optional in snow.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Taxi share only; no fee for the path.

signatureExperiences.title: Kekova's sunken city by local boat
signatureExperiences.description: Three hours over drowned Lycian stairs and walls, then up to Simena castle.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Ruins visible beneath the surface, in a quiet sheltered sound.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Haggle with a local captain in the village; about EUR 90 per boat.
signatureExperiences.costNote: EUR 90 per boat split four ways, estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Tent nights at Çıralı and the Chimaera flames
signatureExperiences.description: Pitch in a pension garden and walk to the gas flames after dark.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Fire that has burned from the rock for millennia, reached on foot at night.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book two tent nights at a camping pension; carry head torches.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Two nights at EUR 9 plus entrance, estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Two Pisidian mountain cities, Termessos and Sagalassos
signatureExperiences.description: A steep ruin walk at 1,000 m then a plateau city at 1,500 m near the snowline.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Two of Anatolia's best-preserved highland cities, nearly empty in March.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Drive both from Antalya; check snow and road access the day before.

travelStyle.summary: A self-drive route with daily walks, three tent nights, and guesthouse nights elsewhere.

transport.summary: One rental car picked up at Dalaman and dropped at Antalya, with taxis and a local boat as the only other transport.

modes.description: Two licence holders share the driving; the car carries gear for four.
A negotiated half-day on Kekova Sound.

transport.carRental: Available at Dalaman and Antalya airports from international and local firms. Expect a minimum age of 21–25, a licence held for 1–2 years, a card deposit and a one-way fee; confirm additional-driver terms when booking.

drivingRequirements.summary: Main roads are paved. The D400 coast road is narrow and bendy; Taurus roads can be icy. Drive in daylight.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Conditional on licence country. The UK guidance asks for a 1968 IDP; EU licences are normally valid for short stays; confirm with the rental firm before booking.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences; both should be registered as drivers.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody rides a scooter or motorcycle without the required licence; use the car, taxis, dolmuş and boats.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: One car, two registered drivers, short driving days, and a taxi for one-way walks.

accommodation.summary: Family pensions and guesthouses, with three tent nights in camping pensions.

camping.summary: Camping pensions at Patara and Çıralı take tents in low season; wild camping in national parks and protected areas is not recommended.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Walks of 3–5 h with climbs of about 400 m and steep ruin tracks; cold weather above 1,000 m.

itinerary.summary: Thirteen days: Dalaman, Fethiye, Faralya, Patara, Kaş, Üçağız, Çıralı, Antalya, Ağlasun, Eğirdir, Antalya, with two flexible days for snow and weather.

days.title: Fly in, collect the car, reach the Lycian coast
activities: Fly Paris CDG to Dalaman (one stop, usually Istanbul), arriving mid-afternoon
Collect the rental car at Dalaman airport; both licence holders registered as drivers
Drive 55 km to Fethiye, change money, buy SIM and supplies for the camping nights
Dinner at a lokanta in Fethiye's old quarter
days.accommodation: Guesthouse or pension in Fethiye, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Fethiye's rock tombs of Amyntas are visible above the town
days.practical: Pick-up requires licence, card for deposit; check one-way drop-off fee at Antalya before signing.

days.title: Ölüdeniz to Faralya on the Lycian Way
activities: Drive the car to Faralya first and leave it at the guesthouse; take a taxi to Ölüdeniz
Walk the Lycian Way stage Ölüdeniz–Faralya: about 4 h, about 12 km, with a climb of roughly 400 m on the cliffs above the sea
Optional: Babadağ cable car (to about 1,700 m) or tandem paragliding at Ölüdeniz in place of the walk
Sunset over the Kabak and Butterfly valleys from the guesthouse terrace
days.culturalHighlight: Lycian-era villages of the Faralya plateau
days.geographicalHighlight: Limestone cliffs plunging 400 m to the sea; Babadağ rising to about 1,970 m
days.practical: The stage is waymarked red and white. In March low parts can be muddy; skip the cliff sections in heavy rain.

days.title: Saklıkent, Xanthos and Letoon to Patara
activities: Drive 55 km inland to Saklıkent Gorge; walk the first walkway section and, if the water level allows, the lower reach on foot
Visit Xanthos, the Lycian capital, and Letoon sanctuary (World Heritage property)
Arrive Patara by late afternoon; walk the Roman ruins and the first stretch of the dunes
Camp or pension in Patara
days.accommodation: Campsite or pension in Gelemiş/Patara (tent night 1)
days.culturalHighlight: Xanthos, Letoon and the Lycian League heritage
days.geographicalHighlight: Saklıkent Gorge cut into the Akdağ massif
days.practical: March meltwater can close the gorge; the lower reach is on foot in cold water. Keep Saklıkent as a short stop if it is shut.

days.title: The beach, the ruins, then the coast road to Kaş
activities: Morning on Patara's beach and dunes (a protected nesting beach) and the ruins with their Roman granary and lighthouse
Drive the 75 km coast road via Kalkan to Kaş
Walk the Lycian Way near Kaş for 2–3 h with views to the Greek island of Meis
Dinner at Kaş harbour
days.accommodation: Pension in Kaş old town, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Lycian rock tomb in the town and the ancient theatre
days.practical: The D400 coast road is narrow and winding; drive in daylight.

days.title: Kekova's drowned city by boat
activities: Drive 40 km to Üçağız village
Hire a local boat with captain for 3 h (about €90 for the group) over the sunken Lycian remains and to Simena castle at Kaleköy
Walk up to the castle and the rock-cut tombs of Üçağız
Fish dinner in the village; quiet in March
days.accommodation: Family pension in Üçağız, 2 twin rooms
days.geographicalHighlight: Kekova Sound and its sheltered inlets
days.practical: Swimming and diving over the sunken ruins are prohibited; a sea kayak or boat is the legal way to see them.

days.title: Myra and the road to the Chimaera
activities: Visit Myra rock tombs and theatre, and the Church of St Nicholas in Demre
Continue 100 km via Finike to Olympos/Çıralı
Pitch tents at a camping pension in Çıralı
After dark, walk with head torches to the Chimaera flames (about 40 min each way on a stepped path)
days.culturalHighlight: Myra's carved tombs and Byzantine pilgrimage church
days.geographicalHighlight: Natural gas flames on Mount Chimaera
days.practical: The evening walk is lit only by head torches; carry two per person and keep to the path.

days.title: Olympos in the forest, Lycian Way to the sea
activities: Walk to the ruins of Olympos, a Lycian city in a forested valley, and out to its beach
Lycian Way stage between Çıralı and Adrasan side, or a half-day on the pebble coast
Rest afternoon and a second tent night
Dinner at a family-run pension
days.geographicalHighlight: Beydağları coastal park, pine forest to shoreline
days.practical: A slow day on purpose, after three long days. Entry to the Olympos site and the Chimaera is charged separately.

days.title: To Termessos, a mountain city that was never taken
activities: Drive 100 km north to Antalya then 35 km west to Güllük Dağı National Park
Climb through the ruins of Termessos at about 1,000 m: theatre, agora, necropolis; allow 3 h
Evening in Antalya's Kaleiçi old quarter
Dinner at a local lokanta
days.accommodation: Pension in Kaleiçi, Antalya, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Termessos, which resisted Alexander in 333 BCE
days.geographicalHighlight: Güllük Dağı National Park, pine and cedar
days.practical: March can be cool and damp at 1,000 m; wear layers. The upper site is steep with loose stone.

days.title: Up into the Taurus to Sagalassos
activities: Drive 115 km via Isparta to Ağlasun village
Visit Sagalassos at about 1,500 m: the upper agora, Roman baths, the fountain house, Antonine nymphaeum
Local meal in the village
Check road and weather for the Eğirdir section
days.accommodation: Village guesthouse in Ağlasun, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Sagalassos, a major Pisidian city excavated since 1990
days.geographicalHighlight: Mount Akdağ and the Western Taurus
days.practical: If snow closes the site road, swap with day 11 or skip; the village alone is worth the night.

days.title: Lake District: Kovada and Eğirdir
activities: Drive 70 km via Isparta to Eğirdir; stop at Kovada Lake National Park
Walk Eğirdir's old quarter on its peninsula and the Dilkusha castle area
Short walk or ride on a St Paul Trail section near the lake if snow permits
Lake fish dinner
days.accommodation: Lakeside guesthouse in Eğirdir, 2 twin rooms
days.practical: Nights below freezing are possible; no tents in this part.

days.title: Flexible day for weather, walking or rest
activities: Choose: a St Paul Trail stage near Eğirdir, a boat on the lake, or catch up on delays from earlier days
Laundry, repairs and a long lunch
Use as a buffer if snow, rain or a closed road moved earlier days
Evening walk on the causeway
days.accommodation: Lakeside guesthouse in Eğirdir, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Local fishing community and lake culture
days.practical: Held free on purpose; do not pre-book anything for this day.

days.title: Back to the Mediterranean and the museum
activities: Drive 185 km to Antalya via the Isparta road
Return the rental car at the airport (check the fuel level and one-way fee)
Antalya Archaeological Museum and a last walk through Kaleiçi
Pack and prepare for an early flight
days.culturalHighlight: Antalya museum collection of Pisidian and Lycian finds
days.practical: Allow time for the car return; a taxi to the airport is cheap.

days.title: Fly home
activities: Taxi to Antalya Airport
Fly Antalya to Paris CDG (one stop usually)
Arrive in the evening
days.practical: Check flight times against the Turkish advice for the day; carry insurance papers.

security.summary: The assessed route lies in Muğla, Antalya, Isparta and Burdur provinces, more than 500 km from the Syria border. No official source names it as restricted, and the segments that would have crossed restricted zones (Şanlıurfa, Mardin, Göbekli Tepe, Nemrut) were dropped. It stays conditional because the FCDO says the risk of sudden escalation of the regional conflict is high, and France reported an Iranian missile intercepted near Hatay in March 2026.
security.assessedRoute: Dalaman, Fethiye, Faralya, Xanthos, Patara, Kaş, Üçağız, Myra, Çıralı, Termessos, Antalya, Sagalassos (Ağlasun), Eğirdir, Antalya airport. Outside the assessed route: Hatay, Kilis, Gaziantep, Şanlıurfa, Mardin, Diyarbakır, Batman, Siirt, Şırnak, Hakkari and all Syria, Iraq and Iran border areas.

advisories.level: Yellow (vigilance renforcée) for the whole assessed route; orange for Hatay, Kilis, Gaziantep, Şanlıurfa, Mardin, Diyarbakır, Batman; red for the immediate Syria and Iraq borders
advisories.regionsAffected: South-east and the Syria/Iraq borders; Hatay noted for regional escalation risk
advisories.routeImpact: No route province is orange or red; the proposed Şanlıurfa and Mardin legs were removed.

advisories.level: Against all travel within 10 km of the Syria border; no restriction named for the route; regional tensions: risk of sudden escalation is high
advisories.regionsAffected: Syria border zone; Hatay roads; permits in Hakkari and Ağrı
advisories.routeImpact: Route is clear of named areas; flights and airspace could be disrupted at short notice.

advisories.level: Yellow for the route; orange for Şırnak, Hakkari and Habur; red for the Syria and Iraq border areas
advisories.routeImpact: No orange or red region on the route.

advisories.level: Level 2 – Exercise increased caution; do not travel to the border region with Syria and Iraq
advisories.routeImpact: Route is outside the do-not-travel area.

conflictRisk.note: The route is far from active fighting, but a regional conflict involving Iran has already produced one intercepted missile near Hatay and flight disruption across the region; the situation is described as unpredictable.

terrorismRisk.note: Attacks are mostly reported in the south-east, Ankara and Istanbul; the route avoids those areas but Antalya's airport and tourist places are generic targets.

kidnappingRisk.note: No kidnapping advice for the Lycian coast or Lake District was found in the reviewed sources.

regionalRestrictions: Do not enter the 10 km Syria border zone, Hatay, Şanlıurfa, Mardin, Diyarbakır, Batman or any red or orange province.
Military zones and the Iran/Iraq borders are outside this route.
Wildfire alerts were issued in southern Turkey in summer 2026.
ordinaryRisks: Road accidents on narrow coast and mountain roads
Pickpocketing in cities and strong drug laws
Cold and storm weather above 1,000 m, flood water in gorges
security.medicalAccess: Good private and public hospitals in Antalya and Fethiye; basic care in villages. EHIC is not valid in Turkey per FCDO.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Insurers may exclude cover if travelling against official advice; the route avoids restricted zones but read war and escalation clauses and trekking cover.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; move to eligible only if the FCDO escalation wording and the Iran conflict ease, and downgrade if any route province turns orange or airspace closures return.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality. UK guidance gives 90 days visa-free; EU passport holders are normally visa-free for short stays; other nationalities should check the official e-visa portal. Not assumed.
practicalRequirements.entry: Passport with blank pages; return ticket; customs rules on drugs and e-cigarettes are strict.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: UK guidance says at least 150 days after arrival; verify for your passport.
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with trekking and evacuation cover; EHIC not valid.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: 4G on the coast; local SIM or eSIM from airport shops; weaker in gorges and mountains.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards accepted in towns; carry cash lira for pensions, boats and village restaurants.
practicalRequirements.medical: Carry personal medicines; pharmacies do not honour foreign prescriptions per FCDO.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Petrol stations frequent on the coast road; fill up before Taurus legs.
